title: Adaptation and mitigation strategies to climate change
competency: Describe adaptation, define mitigation, and differentiate between the two.

keywords.def: Adjustments in ecological, social or economic systems to actual or expected climate change, to reduce damage or use opportunities (IPCC).
Limiting climate change by avoiding and reducing greenhouse gas emissions and by enhancing sinks.
A store that takes up and holds greenhouse gases, such as oceans, forests and soil.
Adaptation that takes place after the initial impacts of climate change have occurred.
Adaptation that takes place before impacts become apparent.
Adaptation that results from a deliberate policy decision.
Changes a system undergoes in response to climate irrespective of any policy, plan or decision.

en.text: The UNFCCC names two responses to climate change. Mitigation limits climate change by avoiding and reducing greenhouse gas emissions, for example burning fewer fossil fuels, and by enhancing sinks such as oceans, forests and soil. Adaptation adjusts ecological, social or economic systems to actual or expected climate change, to moderate damage or use opportunities. In Ethiopia common adaptation strategies are soil conservation, terracing, water harvesting, crop diversification, changing planting dates, planting trees and irrigation. Mitigation got more attention in the past, but adaptation became an urgent priority after the IPCC Third Assessment Report.

en.text: Adaptation is classified by timing, goal and motive. Reactive adaptation happens after the first impacts; anticipatory adaptation happens before impacts appear. Private adaptation is by households and companies; public adaptation is by government. Planned adaptation results from a deliberate policy decision; autonomous adaptation happens without any policy. Natural systems adapt only autonomously and reactively, never in anticipation.

screens.title: Before or after?
screens.ask: A town builds a flood early-warning system before any big flood has come. What kind of adaptation is this?
screens.after: It happens before impacts appear: anticipatory. It is also public.

screens.title: Three pairs of types
paras: Timing: reactive (after the first impacts) or anticipatory (before impacts appear).
Who acts: private (households, companies) or public (government).
Motive: planned (a deliberate policy decision) or autonomous (no policy).
Also: short or long term, localized or widespread.
Natural systems adapt autonomously and reactively; never in anticipation.
